clue.text: Wave plate after food

indicators.note: 'after' puts the word for plate behind the word for food in the answer

parts.note: bran is a cereal husk eaten as food
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Someone waves a plate about once the meal has been served.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to flourish or shake something, such as a weapon, in the air, which is a kind of waving.

clue.text: Uplifting, brilliant book? This writer's flattered

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifting means turning upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ace means brilliant
B is an abbreviation for book
the setter refers to themself as this writer; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A writer is pleased by a cheering review of a great book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flattered' means made to look good, as a dress flatters its wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: If a hat became you, it suited you and showed you at your best, so it flattered you.

clue.text: Speak to adult about fee

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
C, circa, means about
a fee is a cost

explanation.surface: Someone has a word with a grown-up about a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly, so to speak to them.

clue.text: Explorer departs with playboy

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: An adventurer sets off accompanied by a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who circumnavigated the globe, an example of an explorer.

clue.text: Cakes smell nice, finally, in ship

indicators.note: 'in' places the earlier pieces inside the word for ship

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

indicators.note: 'finally' keeps only the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: last letter of nice
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Cakes give off a pleasant smell on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smell nice' suggests a pleasant scent, but pong is a bad smell; the two pieces go between the letters of the ship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is a light cake, so sponges are a kind of cakes.

clue.text: Sailor dispatched miles away?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: A sailor has been sent far off to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles away' is the idiom for someone lost in thought, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daydreaming and not paying attention is called absent, or absent-minded.

clue.text: Fat baker's cooked meal

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked books: falsified, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plump baker has prepared a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

clue.text: Former lover was prone, stretched out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to be prone to something is to tend towards it

explanation.surface: An old flame lay flat, stretched out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' seems to mean lying face down, but here it means inclined.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means lengthened or spread out to full length, the same as stretched out.

clue.text: Think highly of nurse? Almost certainly

indicators.note: 'almost' means not quite all, so the last letter of the word before is cut

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to treat them
sure is an informal yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Asked if they admire a nurse, someone answers that they nearly do.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure someone is to value and cherish them, so to think highly of them.

clue.text: Chicken also following a parrot

indicators.note: 'following' puts the word for also after the article a

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken
taken as written
also means too

explanation.surface: A chicken trails along behind a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested bird of the parrot family.

clue.text: Understand article's rage

parts.note: to see is to understand
the definite article; the 's is read as 'is', joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: Someone grasps why a newspaper article is so angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, so it serves as the verb rage.

clue.text: A rook on each field

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook
EA abbreviates each; 'on' places it after in a down entry

explanation.surface: A rook bird perches on every field.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or expertise is an area.

clue.text: Courier's seen germs spreading

indicators.note: things spreading scatter about, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A delivery driver has noticed germs spreading around.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is someone who carries messages or packages, a synonym for this word.

clue.text: Family's receiving first of greetings cards

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: kin is family, with the S of the 's

indicators.note: 'first of' keeps only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of greetings

explanation.surface: A family collects greetings cards, say at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes between KIN and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings are court cards in a pack of playing cards, so they are an example of cards.

clue.text: To an extent, Musk is spoiling X

indicators.note: 'to an extent' means only partly, so just part of the run of words is used

parts.note: sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Elon Musk is somewhat ruining X, his social media platform.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the former Twitter, but here it is the cross written at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An X written at the end of a letter or message stands for a kiss.

clue.text: Grew wrinkled below hip

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'below' puts the first word's equivalent underneath the second's

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
wrinkled means creased

explanation.surface: Something grew lined beneath someone's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to grow larger, so increased matches grew.

clue.text: Incompetent American friend united with Republican

indicators.note: 'united with' signals that the pieces are joined together in sequence

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for American
a mate is a friend
U is short for united, as in football club names
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: An inept American's friend has joined forces with a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'united' does double work: it gives U and also joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur as an adjective can mean unskilful or inexpert, so it fits incompetent.

clue.text: Hold tool for cutting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wrestling grip with the legs crossed round an opponent
second meaning: a pair of crossed blades for cutting paper or cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Surface suggests gripping a tool; the first sense is the wrestling hold or gymnastics move named for the crossed legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wrestling grip using crossed legs and the familiar two-bladed cutting implement.

clue.text: Time inside Post Office right next to bank

indicators.note: 'next to' says these pieces sit side by side in sequence

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
R abbreviates right
a ridge is a bank of raised ground

explanation.surface: An hour indoors at a post office beside a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' here is a prison sentence; porridge is British slang for doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which is time spent inside jail.

clue.text: Picks stylish sandwiches over ones with half missing

indicators.note: a sandwich has filling between its slices, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: chic means stylish
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: 'half missing' means the first half of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing half

explanation.surface: A fashionable sandwich shop chooses some items, half of them missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but means holds inside; 'over' is the cricket abbreviation, and the half that goes missing is the front half.
explanation.definitionFit: Picks as a plural noun means selections, the same as choices.

clue.text: Expression of shock after son's attempt

indicators.note: 'after' puts the exclamation behind the abbreviation for son

parts.note: S abbreviates son; the 's is read as 'is'
eek is a cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A shocked reaction to a son's effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek to do something is to try or attempt it.

clue.text: Bats stagger backwards

indicators.note: 'backwards' tells you to read the word from end to start

parts.note: to stagger someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Bats lurch around flying in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' is not the animal but slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats and nuts are both informal adjectives for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Adult ran off — no day's ordinary!
Quietly annoyed robber, in the main

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
irate means annoyed

explanation.surface: A thief, mostly, was quietly irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is someone who robs ships at sea, the main being a poetic word for the ocean.

clue.text: Fish start to swim under small rocks

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'under' puts these pieces below the abbreviation for small

parts.note: S abbreviates small
hake is a sea fish

indicators.note: 'start to' keeps only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of swim

explanation.surface: A fish begins swimming beneath little rocks on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake something is to rock it back and forth, so shakes is the verb rocks.

clue.text: Do hit the first ball at Wimbledon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be suitable, as in 'that will do'

definitions.text: hit the first ball at Wimbledon?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the tennis stroke that starts a point

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Serve means to suffice or do, and in tennis it is the stroke that puts the ball into play.

clue.text: Found his table's wonky

indicators.note: something wonky is askew, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that his table is unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is not the past of find but the verb meaning set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, which is to establish it.

clue.text: Game birds with black on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'on top' places this letter first, above the rest

parts.note: B abbreviates black, as on pencils
owls are birds

explanation.surface: Game birds with dark crowns on their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase, but Game is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls is a British lawn game of rolling weighted balls towards a small target ball, the jack.

clue.text: Most senior doctor told he's leaving hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order
something leaving departs, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: the letters to be worked on
H is the abbreviation for hospital, on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A senior doctor informs a patient he is being discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb to tamper; H leaves the letters before they are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior person is the one of greatest age, the oldest.

clue.text: What could be ward's disadvantage

parts.note: setter's reading: the word ward, read back to front, is described by the answer
surface reading: a downside of a hospital ward

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the downside of a hospital ward might be.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ward back to front and you get DRAW, so the answer, split as DRAW BACK, describes ward itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or downside, a straightforward synonym of disadvantage.

clue.text: Horses use the leads so regularly

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Advice to lead horses on reins rather than ride them.
explanation.definitionFit: Steed is a literary word for a horse, especially one ridden.

clue.text: US general's gathering large crowds

indicators.note: gathering means drawing something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: George Custer was the US general of Little Bighorn, with the S of the 's
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: An American general is mustering huge masses of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusters means groups gathered closely together, so as a verb it matches crowds.
